If there is fetal malposition, immediately correct to normal position. Target delivery within 30 seconds-1 minute. (3) Neonatal resuscitation: immediately after delivery, secure the airway (suction amniotic fluid from the nostrils), thoracic stimulation, mask O2 10-15 L/min as needed, artificial ventilation (nose-mouth seal, 1-second inspiration → 4-second intervals, 20-30 breaths/min); for cardiac arrest, chest compressions 100/min + epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO. (4) Compression with the Madigan squeeze rope for 20 minutes (NMS prevention). [Post-resuscitation management] (5) Foal blood gas: pH <7.20 and lactate >4 mmol/L diagnose severe asphyxia; start HIE/NMS treatment. (6) Fluids: warm lactated Ringer's 4-6 mL/kg/hr, with 5% glucose (maintain 80-150 mg/dL), sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV (pH <7.10), DMSO 1 g/kg IV diluted to 10% (cerebral edema management). (7) IgG measurement: at 8-12 hours of age, recheck at 24 hours of age; if <800 mg/dL, plasma 20-40 mL/kg IV. (8) Antimicrobial prophylaxis (high sepsis risk): ceftiofur 5 mg/kg IM/IV SID, or penicillin 22,000 U/kg IV q6h + amikacin 25 mg/kg IV SID. (9) NMS treatment: anticonvulsants (diazepam 0.05-0.2 mg/kg IV, midazolam CRI 0.02-0.1 mg/kg/hr), nutrition (milk replacer via nasogastric tube 10-15 mL/kg q2h), ophthalmic protection (artificial tears q2-4h). [Mare management] (10) Placental examination: record abnormalities of the decidual surface (inflammation, discoloration, thickening), placental weight (normal 10-11% of body weight; >14% suggests placentitis), chorionic culture. (11) Uterine lavage: at 12-24 hours postpartum, warm saline 2-4 L + oxytocin 10-20 IU to promote evacuation of uterine contents. (12) Antimicrobials: continue antibiotics for placentitis (TMS 30 mg/kg PO BID + fluconazole 2.5 mg/kg PO SID for 14 days). (13) Laminitis prevention: ice baths for 24-72 hours, phenylbutazone 2.2 mg/kg IV BID (short-term), flunixin 1.1 mg/kg IV BID. [Prognosis] With early incision (within 5 minutes of CA exposure) + successful resuscitation, foal survival rate is 60-80%; 30-40% of long-term surviving foals have HIE sequelae. With delayed intervention (>10 minutes), survival rate is 20% or less. When placentitis is the cause, recurrence in the next pregnancy is high; endometrial examination and culture before breeding are essential. [References] Macpherson Equine Vet J 2009; LeBlanc et al. Theriogenology 2012; Vaala AAEP Proceedings 2003; Equine Reproduction 2nd ed (McKinnon et al. 2011) Ch.226-229; Knottenbelt Equine Neonatal Medicine 2004 Ch.6.
entries.horse|Pyloric Ulceration: [Diagnosis] Gastroscopy confirms circular/linear deep ulcers, cicatricial contraction and stricture around the pylorus. Assess delayed gastric emptying with the 13C-octanoic acid breath test or scintigraphy. [Medical therapy (first stage)] Omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO SID × at least 8 weeks + sucralfate 12 mg/kg PO BID-TID on an empty stomach × at least 8 weeks. Misoprostol 5 μg/kg PO BID-TID concurrently from the outset (PGE1 analogue promoting mucosal blood flow; first choice for EGGD). [Improvement of motility] Erythromycin 1-2 mg/kg IV/PO q6h (motilin receptor agonist, promotes pyloric emptying, diarrhoea as an adverse effect), metoclopramide 0.04-0.05 mg/kg/hr CRI (beware CNS adverse effects), bethanechol 0.025 mg/kg SC q8h. [Feeding management] Small frequent feeds (6-8 times/day), wet mash (added water improves flow), grain restriction, 24-hour pasture/hay access, stress reduction (one full rest day per week), discontinue NSAIDs. [Assessment of healing] Repeat endoscopy after 8 weeks. If no improvement, extend medical therapy (a further 8-12 weeks) or add corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05 mg/kg IV SID × 5 days, tapering). [Surgical indications] Failure of 12-16 weeks of medical therapy, pyloric stenosis (gastric emptying time >4 hours), chronic gastric dilation or continued weight loss: pyloroplasty (Heineke-Mikulicz pyloroplasty) or gastroduodenostomy (Y-U pyloroplasty). Continue maintenance therapy after surgery. [Long-term management] After healing, maintain sucralfate 12 mg/kg PO SID, ongoing management of environmental factors, periodic endoscopy (every 6 months). [Differentials] Gastric adenocarcinoma (older horses), squamous cell carcinoma, gastric diverticulum and cardia stricture also cause similar signs.
entries.horse|Pyrrolizidine Alkaloid Toxicity: No specific antidote — supportive care + hepatoprotection. Immediate removal of PA-containing plants (pasture plant survey and weed control). Fluids: maintain hepatic perfusion, correct electrolytes and acid-base. Dextrose fluids (if hypoglycemic). Hepatic encephalopathy management: lactulose 0.1-0.2 mL/kg PO q8h (reduces intestinal ammonia). Neomycin 15-20 mg/kg PO q8h (suppresses ammonia-producing intestinal bacteria). Vitamin E/Se supplementation (antioxidant). B vitamins. Diet: high-quality roughage; consider low protein (reduces ammonia production). Avoid direct sunlight (photosensitization: phylloerythrin accumulation due to hepatic failure). Prognosis: once clinical signs appear, extensive hepatic fibrosis is irreversible and the prognosis is poor. If ingestion is stopped at the stage of elevated GGT only (asymptomatic), recovery is possible.
entries.horse|Red Maple Toxicosis: [Red maple toxicosis] Oxidative erythrocyte damage → Heinz body hemolytic anemia. Blood transfusion (when anemia is severe, PCV <12%). Ascorbic acid 30-50 mg/kg IV q12h (reducing agent). Fluids (renal protection against hemoglobinuria). Oxygen therapy. Consider N-acetylcysteine. Dried, wilted leaves are the most toxic. Occurs most often in autumn. More severe in mares. Mortality 60-70%.
entries.horse|Renal Failure: [Renal failure in horses] Acute: fluids (lactated Ringer's solution 2-4 L/hr IV) to promote diuresis. Furosemide 1 mg/kg IV. Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (gentamicin, NSAIDs). Electrolyte correction (especially K). Chronic: dietary management (low protein, good-quality forage), fluids (periodic SC). Renal biopsy to evaluate lesions. BUN/Cre/SDMA monitoring. Prognosis depends on the cause and residual renal function.
entries.horse|Renal Tubular Acidosis: [Renal tubular acidosis in the horse] Treatment of the cause (renal disease, drug toxicity, heavy metal toxicosis) is fundamental. Sodium bicarbonate supplementation (150-300 mEq IV slow → oral maintenance, to correct bicarbonate loss). Fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's solution). Management of electrolyte balance (especially K+ correction). BGA (blood gas analysis) monitoring (q6-12h, to assess the degree of metabolic acidosis). Renal function assessment (BUN/Cre/urine specific gravity/GFR). Rare disease → specialist work-up required. Prognosis depends on the underlying disease.
entries.horse|Right Dorsal Colitis (RDC): [Diagnosis] Abdominal ultrasonography (right 12th-15th intercostal spaces) shows right dorsal colon wall >6mm (normal <4mm) with hypoechoic laminar thickening. Suspect when serum albumin <2.5 g/dL. Hypoproteinemia (total protein <5.0 g/dL), decreased A/G ratio, anemia, leukocytosis. Peritoneal fluid usually normal (but protein elevated in severe cases). [Immediate discontinuation of NSAIDs] Completely discontinue all NSAIDs (phenylbutazone, flunixin, ketoprofen). If pain management is needed, butorphanol 0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV q4-6h, or lidocaine CRI 1.3 mg/kg IV bolus followed by 0.05 mg/kg/min. [Feeding management (foundation of treatment)] Completely discontinue long-stem roughage (hay) → reduces the fermentative load on the right dorsal colon. Feed pelleted feed (complete pelleted feed) in small, frequent meals 4-6 times/day, gradually reintroducing coarse fiber (2-4 weeks). Avoid alfalfa (excess calcium/potassium). [Mucosal protection] Sucralfate 20 mg/kg PO q6-8h (on an empty stomach; beware drug interactions). Psyllium (Plantago seed husk) 1 g/kg PO SID (mucosal protection, promotes short-chain fatty acid production). Combination products such as CP Powder (psyllium + prebiotics + probiotics, Equine & Canine Vet Nutrition) simultaneously promote mucosal protection (gelation of psyllium) and reconstruction of the gut microbiota, and may be considered as adjunctive therapy in cases with concurrent antimicrobials or chronic course (Landes et al. JEVS 2008/2020, improvement rates reported in observational studies of chronic recurrent colic). [Misoprostol] 2-5 μg/kg PO q8-12h (PGE1 analog improves mucosal blood flow), particularly effective for RDC (Videla et al. EVJ 2014). Contraindicated in pregnant mares. [Corticosteroids (severe cases)] For severe granulomatous type resistant to metronidazole, dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV SID × 3-5 days, taper gradually (use cautiously due to laminitis risk). [IV fluids/colloids] With hypoproteinemia <3.5 g/dL, hetastarch 5-10 mL/kg IV or plasma transfusion. Lactated Ringer's solution 2-4 mL/kg/hr maintenance. [Infection control] Metronidazole 15 mg/kg PO q8h × 5-7 days (adjunct treatment for anaerobes/Clostridium). [Surgical indications] Consider partial colon resection for cases refractory to medical therapy, stricture formation, or recurrent colic (poor prognosis). [Course] Healing requires 3-6 months. Monitor monthly with ultrasonography and serum protein.
entries.horse|Selenium Toxicity: [Selenium Toxicity] Acute: activated charcoal, aggressive fluid therapy, supportive care. ECG monitoring (in acute cases myocardial necrosis → risk of fatal arrhythmia). Chronic (alkali disease): removal of high-selenium feed is the top priority. Hoof and hair changes (hoof rings, hoof wall cracks, alopecia) may be irreversible. Hepatoprotection (SAMe, silymarin). Nutritional management. Hoof care (management of hoof wall cracks). Change dietary selenium content to 0.5 ppm or less.
entries.horse|Severe / Hemorrhagic ESGD (Grade 3: [Diagnostic criteria] Confirm ECEIM grade 3 (large/multiple ulcers) or grade 4 (deep ulcers, active hemorrhage, adherent fibrin clots) on gastroscopy. Chronic anemia (PCV<30%), hypoproteinemia (total protein <5.5 g/dL) and positive fecal occult blood are common. [High-dose treatment] Omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO SID x at least 4-6 weeks (longer than the 28 days used in mild cases), strictly administered on an empty stomach. After repeat gastroscopic confirmation 48 hours before treatment, extend if recurrent or not healed. [Combination therapy] Sucralfate 20 mg/kg PO q6-8h x at least 4 weeks (mucosal coating, pepsin inhibition, protection of bleeding sites), on an empty stomach and 2 hours apart from other drugs. [Injectable acid suppression] In severe cases or when oral administration is difficult, pantoprazole 1.5 mg/kg IV SID (proton pump inhibitor, faster acting), or esomeprazole 0.5 mg/kg IV SID. [Hemorrhage management] With active hemorrhage or severe anemia (PCV<20%), tranexamic acid 10 mg/kg IV slow q8h, blood transfusion (fresh whole blood 10-20 mL/kg). Iron supplementation (iron dextran 5 mg/kg IM q7d). [Management of complications] Emergency laparotomy if perforation is suspected (acute shock, signs of peritonitis). Cicatricial pyloric stenosis on healing is an indication for pyloroplasty. [Husbandry (extremely important)] Complete rest for 1-2 weeks, 24-hour access to grass/hay, alfalfa pellets 1-2 kg/day, complete discontinuation of grain, divided feeding 8-12 times per 1 day, complete removal of stressors (avoid new environments and transport). [Assessment of healing] Repeat endoscopy after 4 weeks; continue high-dose treatment until grade 2 or lower. After complete healing, maintenance with omeprazole 1-2 mg/kg PO SID x 4-8 weeks, then taper. [Prevention of recurrence] Horses that have had grade 3-4 lesions are high risk; permanent husbandry management + intermittent endoscopic surveillance (every 6 months) + prophylactic dosing during stressful events are essential.
entries.horse|Shaker Foal Syndrome (Toxico-Infec: [Most important: early administration of botulism antitoxin] (1) Antitoxin: BotVax-B or an equivalent type B polyvalent antitoxin 30,000-70,000 IU IV slow drip (diluted 5-fold in saline, given over 30-60 minutes, with venous access secured in preparation for anaphylaxis). Administration within 24 hours of onset dramatically improves survival (>80%); 50-60% at 24-48 hours; benefit after 48 hours is limited. In Japan, BotVax-B requires import procedures; consider sourcing through JRA and equine-breeding-region hospitals in Hokkaido and Tochigi. [Supportive care (the mainstay of treatment)] (2) Airway management and respiratory support: (a) maintain recumbent foals in sternal recumbency to prevent airway obstruction, (b) aspirate saliva and gastric contents via nasogastric tube (NG tube) to prevent aspiration, (c) in cases with severe respiratory depression, tracheal intubation (at minimum a nasal tube) + positive-pressure ventilation (IPPV PIP 15-20 cmH2O, PEEP 5 cmH2O, RR 20-30/min, FiO2 30-50%), (d) oxygen supplementation (nasal cannula 5-10 L/min, maintain SpO2 >90%). (3) Nutritional management: because the foal cannot swallow, milk replacer via nasogastric tube 10-15 mL/kg q2-3h (3-5 times more frequently than usual); use concentrated milk according to increased energy requirements; monitor closely for aspiration risk (aspirate gastric contents before feeding, administer slowly); with prolonged course (>1 week), TPN (Total Parenteral Nutrition). (4) Fluids: warm lactated Ringer's solution 4-6 mL/kg/hr, with 5% dextrose (maintain blood glucose 80-150 mg/dL), electrolyte correction (K, Mg). (5) Decubitus ulcer prevention: change position every 4 hours, soft bedding, joint protection pads, rehabilitative passive range-of-motion exercise. (6) Ocular protection: artificial tears q2-4h (loss of blink reflex), erythromycin ointment q6-8h (corneal ulcer prevention), tarsorrhaphy (severe cases). (7) Urinary management: if unable to urinate voluntarily, place a urinary catheter (aseptically), change the catheter every 12-24 hours, antimicrobial prophylaxis against urinary tract infection (ceftiofur 5 mg/kg IM SID). (8) Antimicrobials (for aspiration pneumonia and urinary tract infection): ceftiofur 5 mg/kg IM/IV BID or penicillin-amikacin combination for 7-14 days. [Absolutely contraindicated drugs] (9) Aminoglycosides (streptomycin, gentamicin, amikacin) — worsen neuromuscular blockade → respiratory arrest; use only in emergencies. (10) Tetracyclines — disrupt the intestinal flora and promote C. botulinum proliferation; avoid absolutely. (11) Magnesium sulfate — worsens neuromuscular blockade. (12) Procainamide, quinidine — worsen neuromuscular blockade. [Elimination of intestinal organisms] (13) Cathartics / intestinal decontamination: mineral oil 1-2 L via NG tube (promotes expulsion of intestinal toxin and spores), metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q8h (antimicrobial against anaerobes, suppresses intestinal C. botulinum proliferation, but note effects on the intestinal flora). (14) Probiotics (lactobacillus, Saccharomyces boulardii) to aid recovery of the intestinal flora. [Rehabilitation] (15) Standing support: partial weight support with a sling (harness), standing practice for a few minutes several times daily, maintain joint range of motion. (16) Passive exercise: flexion-extension of all four limbs q4-6h to prevent muscle atrophy. [Monitoring] Respiratory rate, respiratory pattern, SpO2, heart rate, temperature q2-4h; swallowing function (pharyngeal reflex, tongue strength); urination and defecation; decubitus ulcer formation; neurological assessment (pupils, eyelids, body movement). [Prognosis] With early antitoxin (<24h) + intensive supportive care, survival is 60-80%; recovery period 4-12 weeks (regeneration of neuromuscular end plates). With antitoxin given more than 48 hours after onset, survival is <30%. Sequelae: mild muscle weakness and reduced athletic performance persist in some, but most reach normal adulthood and reproductive capacity. Causes of death are respiratory muscle paralysis, aspiration pneumonia, and sepsis. [Prevention] (1) Type B toxoid vaccination of the mare: booster 2-4 weeks before foaling for colostral IgG transfer (2 doses in late gestation, first at 4 weeks + second at 2 weeks prepartum), then annually. Essential in endemic areas (Kentucky, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia, etc.). (2) Type B toxoid vaccination of foals: 2 doses at 2 and 4 months of age (before colostral IgG wanes), in endemic areas. (3) Environmental management: remove decomposing animal carcasses and spoiled feed from pastures, manage soil pH, test groundwater for contamination. (4) Feed management: high-quality oats and hay, avoid moist fermented feeds, discard moldy feed. (5) Individual foal management: early detection of fecal abnormalities (green, watery stool → suggestive of Clostridium infection), early intervention for swallowing abnormalities. [References] Whitlock RH Vet Clin North Am Equine Pract 1996; Wilkins PA et al. Equine Vet J 2002; Knottenbelt et al. Equine Neonatal Medicine 2004 Ch.13; Robinson/Sprayberry Current Therapy 7th ed; AAEP Vaccination Guidelines 2020 (Botulism, Foals); Centers for Disease Control: Botulism Surveillance.
entries.horse|Stachybotryotoxicosis: [Pathophysiology] Toxicosis caused by trichothecene mycotoxins (satratoxins, roridins) produced by Stachybotrys chartarum (a black mold of the family Stachybotryaceae). Develops from ingestion of mold-contaminated feed (straw, hay, silage, especially when damp or rotting). Clinical course: Stage 1 (oral irritation, leukopenia) → Stage 2 (temporary recovery) → Stage 3 (severe immunodeficiency, hemorrhage). Historical large-scale outbreaks recorded in Eastern Europe (former Soviet Union, Ukraine etc.). [Diagnosis] (1) Mold/toxin analysis of feed (HPLC/ELISA): quantification of satratoxins H and G. (2) CBC: leukopenia (both neutrophils and lymphocytes), thrombocytopenia, anemia. (3) Bone marrow examination: hematopoietic suppression. (4) Association of clinical signs with contaminated feed. (5) Necropsy: necrosis of oral and gastrointestinal mucosa, petechiae, lymph node hemorrhage, bone marrow hypocellularity. [Treatment] ① Immediate removal of contaminated feed (most important; stops further exposure). ② Supportive care: IV fluids (LRS 2-4 mL/kg/hr), transfusion (severe anemia, platelets <50,000), plasma infusion (coagulopathy). ③ Bone marrow recovery: Granulocyte-Colony Stimulating Factor (G-CSF) 1-5 μg/kg SC q24h (under investigation in horses), vitamin B12, folic acid. ④ Prevention of secondary infection: penicillin G 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h (against opportunistic infection due to neutropenia). ⑤ Oral lesions: 0.1% chlorhexidine mouthwash BID-TID, topical antibiotic ointment. ⑥ Nutrition: fresh soft feed (nasogastric tube feeding when prehension is difficult). Vitamin C and E supplementation (antioxidant). [Environmental decontamination] Dispose of mold-contaminated feed by deep burial or incineration. Disinfect stables and equipment with 5% sodium hypochlorite. Ref: Puschner B. Mycotoxicoses in horses. Vet Clin NA Equine 2001; Fung F et al. Stachybotrys review. Arch Environ Health 2004
entries.horse|Toxic Nephrosis: [Toxic nephrosis in the horse] Remove the cause (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, toxic plants). Aggressive fluid therapy (IV lactated Ringer's, to maintain renal blood flow). Monitor urine output. Oliguria → furosemide 1 mg/kg IV, mannitol 0.5 g/kg IV. Electrolyte correction. BUN/Cre monitoring q12h. Identifying the cause is the key to treatment. Acute kidney injury may be reversible with early intervention.
entries.horse|Water Hemlock Toxicity: [Water hemlock toxicity] Cicutoxin (GABA antagonist) → violent seizures are characteristic. Seizure management: diazepam 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV; add pentobarbital if ineffective. Securing the airway is the top priority. Activated charcoal (administer via nasogastric tube after seizures are controlled). Fluid therapy. Rhabdomyolysis → renal protection (aggressive fluids to promote myoglobin excretion). Monitor CK and BUN/Cre. Onset 15-60 minutes after ingestion. High mortality and no specific antidote.
entries.horse|Yew Toxicity: [Yew Toxicity] Taxine alkaloids → Na channel blockade → cardiac arrest. Most cases are sudden death (within hours of ingestion) with very little opportunity for treatment. Survivors: activated charcoal (via nasogastric tube), atropine (for bradycardia), lidocaine 2 mg/kg IV bolus (ventricular tachycardia). Be prepared for CPR. Lethal dose: leaves 0.5-2 g/kg. All parts are toxic and remain toxic when dried. No specific antidote. Prognosis extremely poor.
entries.horse|Zinc Toxicosis: [Zinc toxicosis in horses] Removal of the source is the top priority (replace galvanized feeders, fences and water troughs). Chelation therapy: CaEDTA 75 mg/kg IV slow q12h x 5 days (severe cases, diluted in 5% dextrose and given slowly). Fluid therapy (renal protection, enhance excretion). Copper supplementation (correction of secondary copper deficiency caused by zinc: copper sulfate 0.5-1 mg/kg PO). For acute ingestion of large amounts, GI decontamination (activated charcoal 1-2 g/kg PO + mineral oil). Regular monitoring of CBC and biochemistry (liver enzymes, pancreatic enzymes). Chronic exposure → excessive bone proliferation (physeal enlargement), anemia, arthropathy. Confirm diagnosis by serum zinc concentration.

ja_entries.dog|Fading Puppy Syndrome:
【発見から1時間以内の初期対応が生死を分ける】

(1)体温の測定と復温：直腸温を測定（35℃未満=低体温、34℃未満=重篤）。急速な復温は末梢血管拡張によるショックを引き起こすため禁忌。段階的復温：温タオル・ヒートランプ（45〜50cm離す）・インキュベーターで30〜60分かけて35〜36℃まで引き上げ、次いで37〜38℃を目標。低体温子犬にミルクを与えてはならない（腸管が動いていないため胃内発酵→腹部膨満・死亡）。

(2)低血糖の補正（体温が35℃以上になってから）：5〜10%ブドウ糖液0.5〜1.0 mL/100g体重を経口投与（舌下に少量ずつ）または皮下投与（SC）。改善なければ静脈路確保（外側伏在静脈または骨髄路）し2.5〜5%ブドウ糖加乳酸リンゲル液で維持。目標BG>70 mg/dL。

(3)脱水・電解質：皮下輸液（乳酸リンゲルを温めて30〜40 mL/kg/日に分割、皮下）または経口補液（新生子専用ORS）。重症脱水は静脈路確保の上LRS 10〜15 mL/kg/hr。

(4)感染の除外と治療：臍帯消毒（出生時：10%ポビドンヨード浸漬）。敗血症疑いには広域抗菌薬—アモキシシリン15〜20 mg/kg PO/SC q12h（腸内細菌カバー）またはアンピシリン20〜30 mg/kg SC q8h。フルオロキノロン系は関節軟骨毒性のため新生子に使用しない。CHV-1疑い（同腹複数仔の急死、母犬の外陰部水疱）：環境温度を32〜35℃に維持（ウイルスは38℃以上で増殖抑制）。アシクロビル（5 mg/kg SC q8h）は試みられることがあるが、証拠は限定的。

(5)哺乳と栄養：復温・低血糖補正後に哺乳を試みる。吸乳力が弱い場合はカテーテル（フランス5-8号）で胃管栄養—母乳または犬用代用乳（ペットミルク）を体重1g=0.13〜0.2 mLで2〜3時間毎。過剰投与（>5 mL/100g/回）は誤嚥と腹部膨満の原因になるため注意。

(6)先天異常の確認：口蓋を触診（口蓋裂）、肛門の開口確認（鎖肛）、心雑音聴診（先天性心疾患）。外科的矯正が不可能な重篤先天異常では安楽死を選択肢に入れる。

(7)体重モニタリング：出生時体重を記録し、毎日同時刻に計測。生後24時間以内に出生体重の10%増加が必須。12〜24時間体重増加なし=緊急介入の指標。生後1週間は毎日5〜10%増加を目安とする（Mila et al. 2015）。
[ECVN:Block] [PR / Sponsored — not standard treatment — Equine & Canine Vet Nutrition (caninevet.jp)]
• MSM + Amino Complete (high-dose MSM + essential amino acid blend): tissue repair, muscle maintenance, hepatic/renal nutrition
• Booster & Relax (adaptogens + B-complex vitamins): post-viral convalescence, endocrinopathy energy support, senior fatigue
Note — MSM + Amino Complete: caution: protein load in severe hepatic/renal failure
ja_entries.dog|Neonatal Puppy Mortality / Perinatal:
【時間軸に沿った対応】

(1)分娩直後（0〜2時間）の蘇生：
・気道確保（球状吸引器で鼻/口咽頭を吸引、振り回し禁忌—頭蓋内出血リスク）
・タオルで活発に刺激（30〜60秒）→皮膚の赤み・発声・自発呼吸の回復を確認
・呼吸停止：マスク/チューブ酸素投与、胸骨圧迫100〜120回/分、ドキサプラム1滴（0.1〜0.5 mg）舌下（慎重に、頻脈誘発に注意）、エピネフリン0.01 mg/kg 気管内または臍帯静脈IV
・復温：35〜37℃まで段階的に加温
・ナロキソン：母犬にオピオイド使用→仔に0.01〜0.04 mg/kg SC/舌下（呼吸抑制解除）

(2)体重測定・記録（出生時と毎日）：
全仔の出生時体重を記録。LBW/VLBW仔を特定し優先的に監視。体重増加基準（生後1週間は毎日5〜10%増）を下回る仔は直ちに補助給餌。

(3)初乳管理（出生後1〜2時間以内が最重要）：
初乳摂取を確認（吸乳行動と乳頭への接触を観察）。泌乳不全・仔が弱い場合は搾乳初乳またはウシ初乳（0.5〜1.0 mL/100g PO）を投与。生後24時間以降は腸管透過性低下により受動免疫移行効率が急落。

(4)低体温・低血糖の管理：フェーディングパピー症候群の治療に準ずる（体温確認→復温→低血糖補正→哺乳の順）。

(5)臍帯管理：出生後速やかにポビドンヨード10%で消毒・乾燥。臍帯炎（発赤・膿汁・腫脹）は広域抗菌薬（アモキシシリン15〜20 mg/kg SC q12h）で治療。

(6)感染症対応：CHV-1疑い（同腹複数仔の急死）は環境温を32〜35℃に保つ（ウイルス増殖抑制）。消毒は塩素系（次亜塩素酸0.5%）が有効。腸炎（下痢・体重減少）はスメア・PCR・糞便検査で原因特定、対症療法（補液・整腸）＋原因別治療。

(7)死亡仔の病理解剖：同腹内で複数死亡する場合は病理解剖（剖検）を推奨—原因特定により生存仔の管理改善と次産次の予防につながる。剖検は冷蔵（凍結しない）で獣医病理学施設に搬送。
[ECVN:Block] [PR / Sponsored — not standard treatment — Equine & Canine Vet Nutrition (caninevet.jp)]
• Kamide Milk (highly digestible liquid nutrition): anorexia, critical-care feeding, enteral/tube feeding
Note — Kamide Milk: contraindicated in complete obstruction; use low-fat version in severe pancreatitis
ja_entries.horse|Eyeworm Disease: 【診断】細隙灯生体顕微鏡で結膜嚢・瞬膜下・涙管内の白色糸状虫体(Thelazia lacrimalis、1-2 cm長)直接確認が診断確定。耳介眼瞼神経ブロック後に鎮静下で結膜を翻転、瞬膜後面・上下円蓋部を徹底探索(複数匹寄生多い)。結膜嚢洗浄液(生理食塩水)を顕微鏡検査で幼虫確認。副次的所見としてフルオレセイン染色で続発性角膜潰瘍評価。併発結膜炎・涙嚢炎評価。流行期(夏季・晩夏)の吸血ハエ(Musca autumnalis・face fly)曝露歴聴取。【治療】機械的除去：生理食塩水で結膜嚢洗浄、鉗子で虫体摘出(細長いmosquito forceps)。駆虫薬：イベルメクチン0.2 mg/kg PO(標準駆虫量)、モキシデクチン0.4 mg/kg PO、反復投与は14日後(成虫・幼虫両段階)。局所ネオスチグミン0.5%点眼(Eulimene滴眼、旧療法)、局所抗菌薬(クロラムフェニコール1% q6h×7日)で続発細菌感染予防、続発性角膜潰瘍にアトロピン1% q12h。全身ivermectin/moxidectin定期駆虫プログラム。【予防】夏季fly mask装着、厩舎のハエ対策(permethrin spray、fly traps)、放牧地の馬糞管理(ハエ繁殖抑制)、群管理で定期駆虫(春夏)。【予後】駆虫・機械的除去で>95%良好、治療遅延例で瘢痕性結膜炎・慢性涙嚢炎残存、角膜障害は時に永続、再感染は予防不十分で多発。【参考文献】Lyons et al. ja_entries.horse|Fescue Toxicosis (Reproductive):

ja_entries.horse|Hepatic Encephalopathy:
【病態】肝機能不全による中枢神経症候。肝不全時の未処理アンモニア・芳香族アミノ酸・GABA様物質等の'毒素'が脳血液関門通過 → 神経伝達異常 → 意識障害・行動異常。血中アンモニア>60 μmol/L(正常<35)、肝細胞機能>70%喪失時に発症。急性型(Theiler病・急性中毒)数日で進行、慢性型は緩徐。致死率50-80%(基礎肝疾患と重症度に依存)。【診断】神経症状のスペクトラム:軽度(HE Grade 1-2):行動変化、沈鬱、食欲変動、軽度運動失調。中等度(Grade 3):頭押し付け(head pressing、特徴的)、円形歩行、盲目様行動、過度発声、無反応、軽度痙攣。重度(Grade 4):昏睡、痙攣、起立不能、瞳孔反射低下。肝疾患証拠:血液生化学(GGT・AST・SDH上昇、ビリルビン>5、胆汁酸>50、低血糖、低アルブミン、PT/PTT延長)、血中アンモニア>60 μmol/L(強相関)、腹部超音波、肝生検(凝固時間正常確認後)。他の神経疾患鑑別(WNV、EPM、脳炎、低血糖、EMS、鉛中毒)。【急性期治療(静穏環境必須)】(1)刺激最小化:暗室・静寂、ヘルメット装着(頭押し付けで自傷)、低血糖予防。(2)IV輸液 LRS+5-10%デキストロース 2-4 mL/kg/hr(低血糖予防必須、目標血糖>80 mg/dL)。(3)腸内アンモニア低下(最重要治療):ラクツロース 0.3 mL/kg PO q6-8h(腸内pH低下→アンモニアイオン化→排出、浸透圧性便促進)、反応なければ用量調整(最大0.5 mL/kg)、反対に過量で下痢・脱水・電解質異常。ネオマイシン 10-15 mg/kg PO q6h × 3-5日(ウレアーゼ産生菌抑制、腎機能監視:腎毒性リスク)。メトロニダゾール 15 mg/kg PO q8h(嫌気性菌抑制、HE改善補助、ネオマイシン代替または併用)。(4)分枝鎖アミノ酸(BCAA):経静脈的または経口でBCAA/芳香族アミノ酸比を増加させる、理論的根拠(馬での明確なエビデンス限定)。(5)脳浮腫対策(重度HE):マンニトール 0.25-1 g/kg IV slow × 30分、反復可、頭蓋内圧低下(Divers et al. 2011推奨)。【痙攣・興奮管理】ジアゼパム 0.02-0.1 mg/kg IV(最低用量から、呼吸抑制警戒)、フェノバルビタール 5-10 mg/kg IV/PO SID(肝代謝のため慎重)、キシラジン禁忌(HE悪化・低血圧)。ミダゾラム 0.02-0.1 mg/kg IV slow(短時間作用)。【食事療法】低蛋白(8-10%)、分枝鎖アミノ酸比率高、イネ科牧草のみ(アルファルファ・高蛋白禁忌)、ビートパルプ+穀類少量を頻回、経口摂取不能時は鼻胃管粥またはPPN(アミノ酸は標準よりBCAA高比率を選択)。【基礎肝疾患治療】dg_liver_failure参照。急性肝不全:原因特定と治療、慢性:免疫抑制(デキサメタゾン)。【凝固障害】ビタミンK1 0.5-1 mg/kg IM q24h × 3日、新鮮凍結血漿 2-6 L(活動性出血)、出血予防(圧迫)。【予後指標】(Durham & Smith-Maxie EVJ 2014)継続するアンモニア>100、ビリルビン>10上昇、Grade 4 HE、昏睡、反復痙攣 → 予後不良。Grade 1-2の早期治療で30-50%生存、急性Theiler病40-60%生存可能性。参考:Durham AE. Hepatic encephalopathy in horses. EVE 2005;Divers TJ. VCNA Equine Pract 2011。

ja_entries.horse|Internal Parasites: 【診断】糞便虫卵計測(FEC、McMasterまたはMini-FLOTAC法)で250-500 EPG以上をhigh shedder、200未満をlow shedderと区分(AAEP Internal Parasite Control Guidelines 2019)。小円虫幼虫型(cyathostominosis)疑いは血清フィブリノーゲン・アルブミン・腹部エコーで評価。条虫はELISA血清抗体または糞便PCR(虫卵検出感度低)。【選択的駆虫(AAEP推奨)】high shedder馬のみ年2-3回駆虫し、低耐性集団を温存。【第一選択薬】モキシデクチン 0.4 mg/kg PO(円虫成虫+幼虫型に有効、24時間以内に虫体排出、作用期間12-16週)、またはイベルメクチン 0.2 mg/kg PO(円虫成虫、8-10週)。【条虫対策】プラジカンテル 1 mg/kg PO(Anoplocephala perfoliataに有効)をイベルメクチン/モキシデクチンと合剤で年1-2回(秋)。【幼虫型小円虫症(larval cyathostominosis)】モキシデクチン 0.4 mg/kg PO(粘膜内嚢胞期幼虫に唯一有効)、またはフェンベンダゾール 10 mg/kg PO SID × 5日間(power pac)。重症例には低用量プレドニゾロン 0.5-1 mg/kg PO SID × 5-7日漸減で過剰炎症反応を抑制(Peregrine et al. EVJ 2014)。【支持療法】蛋白漏出性腸症にはIV輸液・血漿輸血、貧血にはダルベポエチン等を適宜。【駆虫抵抗性モニタリング】駆虫14日後のFEC reduction testで90%未満なら抵抗性疑い(Nielsen et al.
